study_name: Meno-J Theory Study 5: Historical J-Jump Casebook 4
case: Continental drift, ocean-floor spreading, and plate tectonics

sources.authors: Alfred Wegener; English translation by Roland von Huene
sources.title: The Origin of Continents
supports: Wegener explicitly proposed horizontal continental displacement as a unifying alternative to fixed-continent accounts.

sources.authors: Alfred Wegener; translated by J. G. A. Skerl
sources.title: The Origin of Continents and Oceans
supports: Wegener combined geometrical, geological, paleontological, paleoclimatic, and geodetic considerations, while proposing physically problematic motion through oceanic substrate.

sources.title: The Earth: Its Origin, History and Physical Constitution
supports: Contemporary geophysical criticism challenged the adequacy of proposed tidal and rotational driving forces and the mechanical behavior required by drift.

sources.authors: American Association of Petroleum Geologists; W. A. J. M. van Waterschoot van der Gracht, editor
sources.title: Theory of Continental Drift: A Symposium
supports: The early controversy contained qualified support, factual disputes, and methodological disagreement—not one uniformly mocking rejection.

sources.title: Radioactivity and Earth Movements
supports: Holmes proposed heat-driven mantle circulation as a possible mechanism connecting internal energy, spreading, and continental movement.

sources.title: Applications of the Remanent Magnetization of Rocks
supports: Paleomagnetism offered an independent physical method for comparing past continental positions and apparent polar-wander paths.

sources.title: Climatic Change through Geological Time in the Light of Palaeomagnetic Evidence
supports: Systematically different continental paleomagnetic paths and paleoclimate indicators supported relative continental motion rather than one shared polar path.

sources.title: History of Ocean Basins
supports: Hess proposed ocean-floor renewal at ridges and return into the mantle, replacing continents-plowing-through-fixed-seafloor with moving oceanic substrate.

sources.authors: Frederick J. Vine and Drummond H. Matthews
sources.title: Magnetic Anomalies over Oceanic Ridges
supports: The magnetic-stripe hypothesis joined geomagnetic reversals to symmetric seafloor accretion and generated quantitative spreading-rate expectations.

sources.authors: Edward Bullard, J. E. Everett, and A. Gilbert Smith
sources.title: The Fit of the Continents around the Atlantic
supports: Least-squares fitting at continental margins quantified Atlantic reconstruction and stated its residual errors rather than relying on coastline resemblance.

sources.title: A New Class of Faults and Their Bearing on Continental Drift
supports: Transform faults supplied a new boundary type whose geometry and earthquake behavior followed from relative plate motion.

sources.title: Deep Earthquake Zones, Anomalous Structures in the Upper Mantle, and the Lithosphere
supports: Deep seismic zones beneath island arcs supported a strong descending lithospheric slab and crustal recycling.

sources.authors: Dan P. McKenzie and Robert L. Parker
sources.title: The North Pacific: An Example of Tectonics on a Sphere
supports: Rigid aseismic regions moving as plates on a sphere predicted boundary slip directions using finite rotations.

sources.title: Rises, Trenches, Great Faults, and Crustal Blocks
supports: Morgan generalized rigid crustal blocks including oceanic regions and connected rises, trenches, faults, and spherical motions.

sources.title: The Rejection of Continental Drift: Theory and Method in American Earth Science
supports: American rejection cannot be reduced to absence of mechanism; disciplinary standards about direct and indirect evidence also shaped appraisal.

sources.title: Rationality and Irrationality in the History of Continental Drift
supports: A theory can be insufficiently warranted for acceptance yet epistemically worthy of continued pursuit; early drift should not have been abandoned as unworthy.

sources.title: The Continental Drift Controversy
supports: The transition developed through distinct paleomagnetic, ocean-floor-spreading, and plate-kinematic research programs rather than a single vindication event.

sources.title: Developing the Theory of Plate Tectonics
supports: Ocean-floor topography, magnetic reversals and stripes, seafloor spreading, rock ages, and earthquake-volcano localization formed a converging evidential system.

sources.title: Cold War and Earth Sciences
supports: Military patronage, new instruments, global surveys, and classification helped create both new ocean-floor knowledge and consequential domains of ignorance.

sources.title: A Harbinger of Plate Tectonics: Commentary on Bullard, Everett and Smith (1965)
supports: The quantitative Atlantic fit was a kinematic bridge between continental drift and plate tectonics, explicitly distinct from a complete driving mechanism.

lineage_nodes.name: Fixed-continent predecessor mosaic
lineage_nodes.component: land bridges, contraction, vertical movements, and regional geology
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: It addressed real stratigraphic, fossil, mountain-building, and isostatic observations through established field practices.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: Separate auxiliary explanations struggled to unify cross-ocean matches, paleoclimates, and later global geophysical patterns.

lineage_nodes.name: Wegener's continental-displacement synthesis
lineage_nodes.component: mobile continents and reconstructed past geography
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: It unified continental-margin fit, matching geology and fossils, and paleoclimatic distributions under relative continental motion.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: Continents were modeled as moving through oceanic substrate under inadequate forces, with rates and reconstructions of uneven quality.

lineage_nodes.name: Interwar appraisal and criticism
lineage_nodes.component: mechanical, evidential, and disciplinary stress testing
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: Critics exposed force-scale, material, fit, and evidential problems that a mature mobility theory had to answer.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: Treating the whole research program as unworthy of pursuit overreached the available counterevidence and ignored its unifying promise.

lineage_nodes.name: Holmes's mantle-circulation mechanism program
lineage_nodes.component: internal heat, convection, upwelling, and horizontal transport
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: It made internal circulation a physically motivated research path and anticipated links among spreading, sinking, and crustal movement.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: It lacked the postwar ocean-floor observations, quantitative plate boundaries, and decisive independent tests required for a complete theory.

lineage_nodes.name: Postwar observability infrastructure
lineage_nodes.component: sonar bathymetry, marine magnetometry, global seismology, dating, and surveys
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: Previously hidden ocean-floor structure became measurable, comparable, and globally mappable.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: Data and instruments did not logically generate one theory; patronage and classification also shaped what was collected and shared.

lineage_nodes.name: Hess's seafloor-spreading architecture
lineage_nodes.component: creation, lateral transport, and recycling of oceanic lithosphere
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: It redefined the moving substrate and connected ridges, ocean-basin youth, trenches, and mantle circulation.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: Initially speculative elements and mechanism details required independent empirical discrimination.

lineage_nodes.name: Independent marine and seismic discriminators
lineage_nodes.component: magnetic symmetry, age patterns, transform geometry, and descending seismic zones
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: Several new observation types tested different consequences of spreading, boundary motion, and recycling.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: No single discriminator supplied the entire global kinematic architecture or resolved all driving-force questions.

lineage_nodes.name: Rigid-plate tectonic synthesis
lineage_nodes.component: lithospheric plates, spherical rotations, and boundary interactions
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: It unified continental and oceanic motion, spreading ridges, subduction zones, transforms, earthquake vectors, and reconstruction rates.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: Plate interiors are approximations and the balance among slab pull, ridge forces, mantle flow, initiation, and deep-time regimes remains research-active.

J2_retention_accounting.reason: Regional geology, fossils, and climate indicators were retained and reassembled, but some reconstructions and force claims failed.

J3_new_reach.reason: One reconstruction linked observations across geology, paleontology, climatology, and geography.

J6_falsifiability_growth.reason: Reconstructions risked mismatch in geology, fossils, climates, and geodesy, though decisive ocean-floor tests were unavailable.

J3_new_reach.reason: Ridges, trenches, ocean-floor youth, sediment patterns, and continental separation entered one cyclic architecture.

J1_representation_change.reason: Oceanic crust became a time-ordered magnetic record and boundaries became kinematically typed structures.

J2_retention_accounting.reason: Margin fit and paleomagnetic mobility were retained while being tied to spreading, transforms, and sinking slabs.

J3_new_reach.reason: The framework predicted stripe symmetry and rates, correct transform sense, deep slab geometry, and quantitative reconstructions.

J4_complexity_dimensions.reason: Several independent datasets became mutually constraining parts of one boundary system.

J6_falsifiability_growth.reason: Each independent data family supplied its own failure surface and cross-checks on rates and directions.

transition_edges.unresolved: A global rigid-plate kinematics still had to close motions consistently on a sphere.

J1_representation_change.reason: Continents and oceanic lithosphere became parts of rigid plates separated by spreading, transform, and subduction boundaries.

J2_retention_accounting.reason: Wegener's relative continental histories, Holmes-Hess mobility, and boundary evidence were recovered within a new moving object.

J3_new_reach.reason: Euler rotations connected slip vectors, spreading rates, transforms, trenches, and reconstructions quantitatively.

J4_complexity_dimensions.reason: A small set of plate rotations compressed global surface motion while idealizing intraplate deformation.

J5_rival_discrimination.reason: Closed spherical motions and boundary-consistent vectors distinguished the synthesis from loose continental mobility.

J6_falsifiability_growth.reason: Predicted velocities, fault senses, boundary locations, earthquake vectors, and reconstruction closure could independently fail.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: Wegener merely noticed that coastlines fit.
false_jump_controls.reason: His case integrated geological, fossil, climatic, geographical, and attempted geodetic evidence.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: Plate tectonics proved Wegener's complete theory correct.
false_jump_controls.reason: Plate theory changed the moving object, rejected plowing and weak forces, and added ocean-floor creation, recycling, and boundaries.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: Early critics were simply irrational conservatives.
false_jump_controls.reason: Mechanical and evidential objections were serious even though abandoning pursuit was not warranted.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: Lack of mechanism alone explains American rejection.
false_jump_controls.reason: Disciplinary evidential standards and methodological preferences also shaped rejection.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: A theory worthy of pursuit should already be accepted as true.
false_jump_controls.reason: Promising unification can justify research before evidence justifies belief or operational adoption.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: Holmes had already completed plate tectonics in 1929.
false_jump_controls.reason: He proposed a fruitful mechanism family without the later oceanic object, boundaries, kinematics, or discriminators.
His architecture created risky predictions whose warrant came from later independent evidence.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: Vine and Matthews alone discovered plate tectonics.
false_jump_controls.reason: Magnetic stripes were one powerful link within paleomagnetic, bathymetric, seismic, fault, and kinematic programs.
Plates can contain both oceanic and continental lithosphere, and some continents span or interact with multiple plates.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: New instruments automatically produced the correct theory.
false_jump_controls.reason: Theory guided interpretation, while patronage, sampling, secrecy, and disciplinary choices shaped the observable record.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: Acceptance in the 1960s settled every mechanism and domain question.
false_jump_controls.reason: Plate kinematics is strongly established while driving forces, diffuse deformation, initiation, and deep-time regimes remain active research areas.

extensions.new_rule: Partition evidence by availability date and issue a contemporaneous verdict before adding retrospective evidence. Never credit a precursor with later instruments, observations, concepts, or successful descendants.
extensions.guardrail: Later vindication can update lineage credit but cannot rewrite the warrant originally available.

extensions.new_rule: Score rejection, non-acceptance, pursuit, provisional use, and acceptance separately. A hypothesis may rationally merit pursuit while rationally failing the acceptance threshold.
extensions.guardrail: Promising is not true; premature non-acceptance is not the same as suppressing further investigation.

extensions.new_rule: Record whether the successor preserves the predecessor's objects or replaces them. If the moving, causal, or measured object changes, treat the relation as transformation rather than simple confirmation.
extensions.guardrail: Shared surface vocabulary such as drift does not establish identity between continents and lithospheric plates.

extensions.new_rule: For each evidential success, record whether it was used to construct, tune, or independently test the proposal, and whether it discriminates against named rivals jointly or only in isolation.
extensions.guardrail: Do not count multiple transformations of one dataset as independent convergence or call post-hoc fit a novel prediction.

extensions.new_rule: Record which claims were untestable under the available measurement infrastructure and which new instruments, surveys, access, funding, or data-sharing changes expanded the falsification surface.
extensions.guardrail: Do not treat infrastructure as automatic truth production; document sampling, classification, and institutional selection effects.

contract_extension.revised_j_jump_object: A hindsight-controlled lineage subgraph with separate pursuit and acceptance verdicts, explicit object identity or redefinition, independently classified predictions, dated observability limits, and a successor architecture that survives cross-domain closure tests.

significant_findings: Wegener's program deserved continued pursuit even though full acceptance was premature; Meno-J must separate those epistemic decisions.
Plate tectonics did not merely add a mechanism to continental drift: it redefined the moving object from continents to lithospheric plates containing continental and oceanic material.
The strongest warrant came from independent cross-domain closure—magnetic symmetry, ages, transform geometry, deep seismic zones, and spherical motion—not from retrospective resemblance alone.
Rejection was historically multi-causal: mechanical objections mattered, but disciplinary standards concerning direct and synthetic evidence also shaped appraisal.
New instruments and surveys expanded what could be falsified; observability infrastructure is therefore part of scientific reasoning, not invisible background.
For AI J-jumps, the target is a pursuit-worthy new representation that states what future observation would make it acceptance-ready, not a confident claim of present truth.
